clue.text: Departed with others heading back

indicators.note: heading back tells us to read the phrase for 'with others' from its end to its start

parts.note: et al is Latin shorthand for 'and others'

explanation.surface: Someone left in a group, all heading home together.
explanation.definitionFit: Departed can mean dead, and the late person is one who has died.

clue.text: Nick a match

explanation.surface: Steal a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Nick is a name for the Devil, also called by the fallen angel's name; the same word was an early brand of friction match.

clue.text: Light appears to diminish gradually

explanation.surface: A light that seems to be slowly fading.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin candle or wick is a light, and to narrow or lessen bit by bit is to diminish gradually.

clue.text: Standstill brought by work on road

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece placed on another comes after it

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a road
OP is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: Roadworks have brought traffic to a halt.
explanation.definitionFit: A complete halt is a standstill, as when traffic comes to a full stop.

clue.text: Article is supporting second proposition

indicators.note: in a down clue a piece supporting another sits beneath it

parts.note: the is the definite article
taken as written

explanation.surface: A grammar point backing up a secondary argument.
explanation.definitionFit: A proposition put forward to be argued and proved, as in a dissertation.

clue.text: Strange training provided by copper, a bent one?

parts.note: PE is physical education, a form of training
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
someone bent is crooked, and a dishonest person who tells untruths fits

explanation.surface: Odd that a policeman, a corrupt one, would be given training.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' suggests a policeman, which makes 'bent' read as corrupt; it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Strange and peculiar are synonyms meaning odd or unusual.

clue.text: Bone right at rear of female bird

indicators.note: at rear of places the letter for right behind the rest of the pieces

parts.note: the emu is a large flightless Australian bird

explanation.surface: The right leg bone at the back of a hen bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The thigh bone is the longest bone in the human body.

clue.text: Game advice from would-be influential editor

explanation.surface: Tips on playing from an editor who wants to sway readers.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half reads as the editor telling readers to follow his leading article, the leader being a newspaper's editorial.
explanation.definitionFit: A children's game in which everyone copies whatever the person in front does.

clue.text: Obstacle put up in lake beginning to restrict duck

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the lake word

parts.note: a mere is a lake

indicators.note: put up in a down clue means the obstacle word is written upwards, backwards

parts.note: a snag is an obstacle or hitch

indicators.note: beginning to takes the opening letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A barrier erected in a lake starts to hem in a duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' reverses SNAG to GANS, placed in MERE; 'beginning to' adds R from restrict.
explanation.definitionFit: A fish-eating diving duck with a serrated bill, also called a sawbill.

clue.text: Runs repeatedly towards sound of blows'

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: repeatedly says the word for towards appears over and over, here three times

parts.note: at can mean towards, as in throwing something at a target
at can mean towards, as in throwing something at a target

explanation.surface: Someone keeps running towards the noise of a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeatedly' gives AT three times, not just twice. The apostrophe after 'blows' is an OCR stray; the page prints 'blows'.
explanation.definitionFit: Knocking on a door makes a quick series of tapping noises, a repeated knocking sound.

clue.text: Reformed addicts end mile what sort of race is it?

definitions.text: what sort of race is it?

indicators.note: reformed, of former addicts, here means the letters of the next three words take a new shape

explanation.surface: Recovering addicts finish a mile and wonder what kind of race they ran.
explanation.definitionFit: Races from 800 metres up to about 3,000 metres, such as the mile, are classed between sprints and long-distance runs.

clue.text: Fancy headgear taken by entertainer

explanation.surface: A fancy hat worn by a performer on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: Caprice was a famous model and entertainer in late-1990s Britain, and her name opens with CAP, a piece of headgear, so the second half is a cryptic pointer to her.
explanation.definitionFit: A fancy is a sudden whim, and a caprice is exactly such a passing notion.

clue.text: Ritual PC worked out when releasing a villain

indicators.note: worked out says the letters of the clue's first two words are rearranged
when releasing says one letter of that pool is let go before the rearrangement is final

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A police constable solves a ritual crime and lets the culprit go.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the letters of RITUAL PC, release A, and rearrange the remaining seven.
explanation.definitionFit: The guilty party in a crime is the wrongdoer, the villain of the piece.

clue.text: An alarming way to drive many out of office

definitions.text: An alarming way to drive many out of office

parts.words: An alarming way to drive many out of office
parts.note: sounds like a coup ousting officials, but describes a practice evacuation triggered by a bell that empties a workplace

explanation.surface: A frightening method of removing many people from power.
explanation.definitionFit: A practice evacuation is set off by an alarm and sends office staff out of the building.

clue.text: Love piece of abstract painting

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, written as the letter O
a piece of something is a part of it

explanation.surface: Someone adores a section of an abstract canvas.
explanation.definitionFit: This 1960s movement made abstract paintings using optical illusions.

clue.text: Noise made by one sort of bat

explanation.surface: A clatter made by a bat swung in a game.
explanation.definitionFit: A din is loud noise, and the strung bat used in tennis or squash goes by the same name.

clue.text: Vocal expression of hypocrisy and a bad temper

parts.note: cant is insincere or hypocritical talk
taken as written
bile is irritability or bad temper

explanation.surface: Someone voices insincere words and a grumpy mood.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical direction meaning in a smooth singing style, a vocal manner of expression.

clue.text: House taken from Thomas More reallocated to primate

indicators.note: reallocated means the letters of the statesman's name are shared out in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the name supplying the letters

explanation.surface: A house confiscated from the Tudor statesman Thomas More is handed to an archbishop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken from' removes HO from THOMAS MORE; the remaining letters rearrange. 'Primate' suggests an archbishop, as befits More's story, but it is the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: This small South American monkey is a member of the primate order.

clue.text: A horde is on the move in the old country

indicators.note: on the move means the letters of the preceding three words shift into a new order

explanation.surface: A marauding horde roams through a former nation.
explanation.definitionFit: The former British colony in southern Africa, now Zimbabwe and Zambia, no longer exists under that name.

clue.text: After a couple of draws, it may be settled in sudden death fashion

definitions.text: After a couple of draws, it may be settled in sudden death fashion

parts.words: After a couple of draws, it may be settled in sudden death fashion
parts.note: reads like a football match going to a sudden-death decider after drawn games, but the draws are of pistols and the death is literal

explanation.surface: A tied contest goes to a sudden-death decider.
explanation.definitionFit: A duel with pistols ends when one shooter falls dead after both draw their weapons.

clue.text: Fabulous creature, one fine female captured in smile

indicators.note: captured in places the three short pieces inside the smile word

parts.note: a grin is a broad smile
I is the Roman numeral for one
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A mythical beast and a lovely woman are caught in a smile.
explanation.definitionFit: A mythical beast with an eagle's head and wings and a lion's body, the stuff of fable.

clue.text: It's a bit of a bloomer printing newspaper without collective wisdom

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside places the newspaper's letters around the rest

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times, a printed newspaper
lore is the traditional knowledge held by a community

explanation.surface: A newspaper prints a howler because it lacks the shared knowledge of its staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' suggests a blunder, but it is a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A small flower forming part of a larger flower head, as in cauliflower or broccoli.

clue.text: Old gaoler here, new in another country

indicators.note: in places the letter for new inside the country

parts.note: Turkey is a country straddling Europe and Asia

explanation.surface: A former prison guard here, new in a foreign land.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnkey was a jailer, the one who turned the keys in prison locks.

clue.text: I am left to find the meaning

parts.note: I am contracts to I'm
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: Someone left behind trying to work out what something means.
explanation.definitionFit: The import of a statement is its meaning or significance.

clue.text: Lacking skill at home, needing a form of training

parts.note: someone who is in is at home
taken as written
PT is physical training

explanation.surface: An inept person stays home and needs some exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsuitable or clumsy, so lacking in the skill or aptness required.

clue.text: English intend to have outwardly austere bearing

indicators.note: outwardly says the word for austere sits on the outside, wrapping the other pieces

parts.note: dour means stern and severe
to mean something is to intend it

explanation.surface: An Englishman sets out to carry himself with a stern air.
explanation.definitionFit: Bearing is the way a person carries and conducts themselves, their manner or deportment.

clue.text: Rambling rose obscuring one sort of branch

indicators.note: obscuring means the rearranged flower covers and hides the letter for one inside it
rambling means the letters of rose wander into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A climbing rose hides a single branch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rambling' turns ROSE into OSER, and 'obscuring' hides I within it. 'Rambling rose' looks like a plant name, but rambling is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A willow shoot or twig used in basket-making is a kind of slender branch.

clue.text: What happens as Sat, begins, comrades?

explanation.surface: A question about what goes on as some sat down together with their comrades.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sat' is not sat down but Saturday: as Saturday begins, Friday ends, so the first half spelt out is FRI ENDS.
explanation.definitionFit: Comrades are companions or pals, people bound by mutual liking.

clue.text: Needle is injected into injured bloke

indicators.note: injected into puts the little word is inside the scrambled letters
injured means the word bloke is damaged into a new letter order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A hospital patient, a hurt man, is given an injection with a needle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'injured' turns BLOKE into OBLEK, the letters that 'injected into' wraps around. The medical picture makes 'Needle' a syringe, but it is a stone pillar like Cleopatra's Needle.
explanation.definitionFit: Tall tapering stone pillars such as Cleopatra's Needle in London are called needles.

clue.text: Relation cuddled by grannie, certainly

indicators.note: cuddled by says the answer is held snugly within the following words

explanation.surface: A family member is surely hugged by her grandmother.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother's or sister's daughter is a family relation.

clue.text: Get her away from completely musical part

indicators.note: away from says the first words are removed from the synonym for completely

parts.note: altogether means completely or entirely
taken as written, the letters to remove

explanation.surface: An order to fetch a woman away from a piece of music.
explanation.definitionFit: The voice part just below the soprano in a choir is a musical part.

clue.text: Play about king in city of Paris

indicators.note: about places the play word around the letter for king

parts.note: to toy with something is to play with it
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A drama about a monarch staged in the French capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paris' looks like France's capital, but it is the Trojan prince whose abduction of Helen started the war.
explanation.definitionFit: Paris was a prince of the ancient city in Asia Minor besieged by the Greeks.
